boundary: Pass 5683 CORRECTS Pass 5673, which claimed W(3,3) is p-rank rigid on the basis of its incidence matrix alone. Pass 5684 proves an upper bound and verifies attainment at q=3 and q=5 only -- it is not proved attained for all q. Pass 5685 REFUTES this pass's own grid-line hypothesis. Pass 5686 refutes a general reading of Pass 5675. Pass 5687 reports an ORDER MATCH and explicitly does not identify the group. Pass 5690 lists what was not done

pass_5683.corrects: Pass 5673's 'W(3,3) is p-rank rigid' -- true of the incidence, false of the adjacency
pass_5683.lesson: the incidence/adjacency distinction was already flagged for Csaszar at Pass 5678 and not applied here until now

pass_5684.note: rank is independent of q while the point count is not
pass_5684.proof: sf is bilinear so sf^2 factors through Sym^2 tensor Sym^2, bounding the rank by dim Sym^2 = 10
pass_5684.statement: rank_q of the non-collinearity matrix of W(3,q) equals dim Sym^2(F_q^4) = 10

pass_5685.hypothesis: the kernel is generated by grid rows and columns
pass_5685.result: REFUTED -- 0 of 60 minimum-weight words is a row or column
pass_5685.still_open: the rook's S4 wr S2, after three failed explanations
pass_5685.why: A r = all-ones for a row indicator r, so rows are not in the kernel

pass_5686.limits: Pass 5675 is not an instance of a general theorem
pass_5686.verdict: a GF(2) kernel does NOT imply imprimitivity -- Petersen and C5 are primitive with nonzero kernels

pass_5687.claim: ORDER MATCH ONLY -- identification is open, one GAP call away

pass_5688.role: exhibits what Pass 5680 showed yosys misses, turning an observation into a constructed object

not_done: yosys beyond the single Reye circuit
pass_5689_5690.standard: the rook's excess 9 and the line graph's 29 are numbers without mechanisms; Pass 5684 shows what a mechanism looks like
